label: Dive
blurb: Wrecks, walls, reefs and pelagics the dive press keeps ranking.

places.name: SS Thistlegorm
places.why: WWII supply ship wreck loaded with motorbikes, trucks and rail cars, one of the world's most-dived wrecks.

places.name: Blue Hole, Dahab
places.why: A sheer 130m sinkhole opening straight onto the reef wall, entered from the beach through a shallow saddle called the Bells.

places.name: Shark and Yolanda Reef
places.why: Two pinnacles at the tip of Sinai with a sheer wall, huge schools of barracuda and jack, and Yolanda's scattered wreck cargo.

places.name: Abu Nuhas Ships' Graveyard
places.why: Four wrecks piled on one shallow reef, sunk over a century of ships missing the same turn into the Suez Canal approach.

places.name: Elphinstone Reef
places.why: A submerged reef wall dropping past 100m on either side of a narrow plateau, known for oceanic whitetip sharks in autumn.

places.name: Daedalus Reef
places.why: An isolated lighthouse reef in open water, walls on every side and a hammerhead shark season that draws liveaboards.

places.name: The Brothers (El Akhawein)
places.why: Two tiny islands rising from deep water with sheer walls, strong currents and two historic wrecks, reached only by liveaboard.

places.name: St. John's Reef
places.why: A maze of coral pinnacles and caves near the Sudanese border, among the least-crowded reef systems in the Red Sea.

places.name: Sanganeb Atoll
places.why: A ring-shaped atoll rising from deep water with a lighthouse on its rim, hammerheads on the plateau and dramatic outer walls.

places.name: Umbria Wreck
places.why: An Italian cargo ship scuttled in 1940 still carrying its wartime load, resting almost intact in clear, shallow water.

places.name: Zabargad Island
places.why: A remote peridot-mining island with pristine reef walls and coral gardens rarely reached outside the liveaboard season.

places.name: Musandam Peninsula
places.why: Fjord-like inlets on the Strait of Hormuz with soft-coral walls, seasonal whale sharks and strong currents from the strait.

places.name: Daymaniyat Islands
places.why: A protected nine-island chain with coral gardens, turtles and a summer whale shark season a short boat ride from Muscat.

places.name: Coral Beach Nature Reserve, Eilat
places.why: The world's northernmost coral reef, shore-accessible with a marked underwater trail through table and brain corals.

places.name: Great Blue Hole
places.why: A near-perfect 300m-wide sinkhole with a ring of shallow reef and a plunge past ancient stalactites at 40m.

places.name: Hol Chan Marine Reserve
places.why: A cut through the barrier reef packed with grouper, snapper and nurse sharks in the adjoining Shark Ray Alley.

places.name: Turneffe Atoll
places.why: Belize's largest atoll, with drop-offs, mangrove flats and calmer diving than the outer reef.

places.name: Palancar Reef
places.why: A drift along Cozumel's signature wall of towering coral pinnacles, swim-throughs and clear Caribbean current.

places.name: Cenote Dos Ojos
places.why: Two linked cenote pools opening into a cavern system of limestone columns and glassy fresh water.

places.name: Cenote Angelita
places.why: A deep sinkhole with a hydrogen-sulphide cloud layer at 30m that looks like a ghostly underwater river.

places.name: MUSA Underwater Museum
places.why: Hundreds of life-cast concrete sculptures sunk to seed new reef and pull divers off the natural reef nearby.

places.name: Cabo Pulmo Reef
places.why: The Sea of Cortez's only hard-coral reef, rebuilt by a no-take zone into schools of jack so dense they blacken the water.

places.name: Los Islotes
places.why: A sea lion colony on a rocky islet where pups play with divers in clear, current-swept water.

places.name: Socorro Island
places.why: A volcanic island three days offshore where giant oceanic mantas approach divers on their own, plus schooling hammerheads.

places.name: Bloody Bay Wall
places.why: A vertical wall starting in 6m of water and plunging past 300m, thick with sponges and famous for its visibility.

places.name: USS Kittiwake
places.why: A submarine-rescue vessel sunk as an artificial reef in 2011, its open decks easy for divers of any level.

places.name: Stingray City
places.why: A shallow sandbar where dozens of southern stingrays gather to be hand-fed, one of the Caribbean's most photographed dives.

places.name: MV Captain Keith Tibbetts
places.why: A Russian Koni-class frigate broken over a reef edge, its bow and superstructure still recognisable at diveable depth.

places.name: Salt Pier
places.why: Pylons of a working salt-loading pier thick with orange tube sponge, dived only when no ship is berthed.

places.name: 1000 Steps
places.why: A shore dive down a cliffside stairway onto a healthy fringing reef, classic Bonaire drive-up diving.

places.name: Saba Marine Park
places.why: Seamount pinnacles rising from deep water around a volcanic island, with pelagics on the outer walls.

places.name: Charles L. Brown Wreck
places.why: A telecom cable-layer sunk as an artificial reef, sitting upright and colonised by soft coral.

places.name: Bianca C Wreck
places.why: A 180m cruise liner that burned and sank in 1961, the largest diveable wreck in the Caribbean, nicknamed the Titanic of the Caribbean.

places.name: Speyside Reefs
places.why: Nutrient-rich Guyana Current diving with the world's largest recorded brain coral and regular manta ray passes.

places.name: Champagne Reef
places.why: Volcanic vents bubble warm gas through the sand like a glass of champagne, alongside a healthy coral slope.

places.name: Silver Bank
places.why: A shallow offshore bank where humpback whales calve each winter, snorkelled rather than scuba dived under strict permit.

places.name: Jardines de la Reina
places.why: A protected archipelago of mangrove cays with some of the Caribbean's healthiest shark populations.

places.name: Cayos Cochinos
places.why: A small marine reserve of cays off Roatán with steep coral walls and some of the region's clearest water.

places.name: Mary's Place
places.why: A dramatic split in the reef wall with narrow canyons of black coral and sponge, one of Roatán's signature dives.

places.name: Utila
places.why: A budget dive hub known for near year-round whale shark sightings feeding on plankton blooms offshore.

places.name: Coiba National Park
places.why: An isolated former penal-colony island with big-animal diving, seasonal whale sharks and schooling hammerheads.

places.name: Cathedral, Providencia
places.why: A cavern of light shafts and swim-throughs off a remote Colombian island closer to Nicaragua than the mainland.

places.name: San Andrés Barrier Reef
places.why: A UNESCO biosphere reef ringing a small Caribbean island, with walls, wrecks and easy drift diving.

places.name: Tiger Beach
places.why: A shallow sandbank in open water where tiger sharks and lemon sharks are reliably encountered without a cage.

places.name: Andros Barrier Reef & Blue Holes
places.why: The world's third-largest barrier reef, riddled with inland and ocean blue holes cut into ancient limestone.

places.name: Thunderball Grotto
places.why: A collapsed limestone cave open to the sky, its underwater tunnels made famous by two James Bond films.

places.name: Bimini
places.why: Shallow banks close to Florida with great hammerhead encounters in winter and resident reef sharks year-round.

places.name: USS Oriskany
places.why: A decommissioned aircraft carrier sunk in 2006, the world's largest artificial reef, its flight deck at 42m.

places.name: USS Spiegel Grove
places.why: A 155m Navy landing ship deliberately sunk off the Keys, big enough to need several dives to see it all.

places.name: Molasses Reef
places.why: The most-dived reef in the continental US, a shallow spur-and-groove system inside the Keys sanctuary.

places.name: Mona Island
places.why: A remote uninhabited island between Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic with pristine walls and few visitors.

places.name: Cane Bay Wall
places.why: A shore-accessible wall dropping from 12m to well past sport-diving limits, dived straight off the beach.

places.name: Bajo Alcyone, Cocos Island
places.why: A seamount 36 hours by boat from the mainland where schooling scalloped hammerheads circle divers on the current.

places.name: Caño Island Biological Reserve
places.why: A jungle-fringed island reserve with rocky reefs, bull sharks and easier access than the Cocos liveaboard run.

places.name: Malpelo Island
places.why: A sheer volcanic rock 500km offshore, walls thick with hammerheads, silky sharks and the odd whale shark.

places.name: Darwin's Arch, Galápagos
places.why: The Galápagos' northernmost dive, a current-swept pinnacle where whale sharks pass overhead from June to November.

places.name: Wolf Island
places.why: A remote pinnacle paired with Darwin's Arch, known for hammerhead schools and strong, cold upwelling currents.

places.name: Devil's Crown
places.why: A submerged volcanic crater teeming with reef fish, sea lions and hammerhead passes in cooler Galápagos water.

places.name: Gordon Rocks
places.why: A flooded volcanic caldera famous for a strong current known as the washing machine and schooling hammerheads.

places.name: Fernando de Noronha
places.why: A volcanic archipelago with the clearest water on Brazil's coast, resident spinner dolphins and green turtles.

places.name: Anacapa Island
places.why: Cold-water kelp forest diving with sea lions and the arches of a small volcanic island off Ventura.

places.name: Browning Pass
places.why: Cold, current-fed water off northern Vancouver Island with some of the world's densest soft-coral walls.

places.name: Silfra Fissure
places.why: A rift between two tectonic plates filled with glacial meltwater so clear visibility runs past 100m.

places.name: Strýtan
places.why: An underwater hot-spring cone rising from the fjord floor, one of the few shallow hydrothermal vents divers can reach.

places.name: HMHS Britannic
places.why: The Titanic's sister ship, sunk in 1916 and lying almost intact at technical-diving depth off a Greek island.

places.name: Zenobia Wreck
places.why: A Swedish ferry that capsized on her maiden voyage in 1980, now one of the world's top wreck-penetration dives.

places.name: Medes Islands
places.why: A no-take marine reserve of seven islets with grouper, moray and a wrecked cargo ship in clear Mediterranean water.

places.name: Blue Hole, Gozo
places.why: A collapsed sea arch dropping through a short tunnel onto open Mediterranean wall, dived straight from the rocks.

places.name: HMS Maori
places.why: A WWII destroyer sunk by bombing, its broken hull lying in shallow water beneath the capital's bastions.

places.name: Plemmirio Marine Reserve
places.why: A rocky Sicilian headland reserve with caves, Roman-era wreck remains and healthy gorgonian gardens.

places.name: B-17 Wreck, Vis Island
places.why: A WWII bomber that ditched in the Adriatic, resting upright and intact on a sandy seabed off a former naval island.

places.name: Port-Cros National Park
places.why: France's oldest marine park, with seagrass meadows, grouper and a wreck trail off a pine-covered island.

places.name: Scapa Flow
places.why: The scuttled remains of the German High Seas Fleet from 1919, giant battleship wrecks in cold, clear water.

places.name: Farne Islands
places.why: A grey seal colony that swims right up to divers among kelp-covered skerries off the English coast.

places.name: Lundy Island
places.why: England's first marine reserve, with kelp forest, wrecks and the country's northernmost sunfish sightings.

places.name: Formigas Islet & Dollabarat Bank
places.why: A seamount between Santa Maria and São Miguel where oceanic manta rays gather over summer.

places.name: Cedar Pride Wreck
places.why: A Lebanese freighter deliberately sunk in the Gulf of Aqaba, now covered in soft coral in warm, calm water.

places.name: Kaş
places.why: Clear Mediterranean water off a laid-back coastal town, with canyons, caves and a WWII fighter-plane wreck.

places.name: Skjervøy
places.why: Fjord waters where orcas and humpback whales corral herring each winter, dived and snorkelled in dry suits.

places.name: Riou Archipelago, Calanques
places.why: Limestone cliffs plunging into the sea south of Marseille, with grouper, octopus and clear inshore water.

places.name: Lofoten Islands
places.why: Cold, gin-clear fjords beneath dramatic peaks, with orca encounters and rich kelp-forest walls.

places.name: Comino Caves & Crystal Lagoon
places.why: Sea caves and a clear turquoise lagoon between Malta and Gozo, an easy, scenic Mediterranean shore dive.

places.name: Aliwal Shoal
places.why: A fossilised sand dune reef known for ragged-tooth sharks in winter and a wreck close by on the same reef.

places.name: Protea Banks
places.why: An offshore reef famous for dense bait balls and one of the most reliable spots to see multiple shark species together.

places.name: Sardine Run, Wild Coast
places.why: An annual migration of billions of sardines that draws dolphins, sharks and gannets into a feeding frenzy divers can join.

places.name: Ponta do Ouro
places.why: A reef-lined coast just north of the South African border with resident whale sharks and manta cleaning stations.

places.name: Tofo Beach
places.why: One of the world's most reliable places to swim with manta rays and whale sharks off an open beach.

places.name: Mnemba Atoll
places.why: A private-island atoll with a steep coral wall and resident green turtles in warm Indian Ocean water.

places.name: Pemba Channel
places.why: A deep channel wall off Zanzibar's quieter sister island, with strong drift currents and pelagic passes.

places.name: Nosy Be
places.why: Volcanic islets with muck-diving critters and a seasonal migration of whale sharks passing the channel.

places.name: Alphonse Atoll
places.why: A remote coral atoll with pristine walls, grey reef sharks and giant trevally in barely-dived water.

places.name: Aldabra Atoll
places.why: The world's second-largest coral atoll, a UNESCO site with tiger sharks and giant tortoises on the surrounding cays.

places.name: Quirimbas Archipelago
places.why: A little-dived chain of coral islands in far northern Mozambique with pristine reef and manta cleaning stations.

places.name: Leven Bank
places.why: A submerged bank in the Zanzibar Channel where schooling hammerheads and eagle rays cross strong currents.

places.name: Bazaruto Archipelago
places.why: Dune-backed islands with dugong, manta cleaning stations and clear channel diving between sandbanks.

places.name: Watamu Marine National Park
places.why: A shallow fringing reef and seagrass reserve on Kenya's coast, calmer and warmer than the reefs further south.

places.name: Hanifaru Bay
places.why: A shallow bay where monsoon currents concentrate plankton, drawing feeding aggregations of dozens of manta rays.

places.name: Maaya Thila
places.why: A coral thila circled by whitetip reef sharks by day and hunted over by them at night, a classic Maldives night dive.

places.name: Vaadhoo Channel
places.why: A current-swept channel between atolls where grey reef sharks and eagle rays stack up on the plateau.

places.name: Hikkaduwa Marine Sanctuary
places.why: A shallow coral garden reserve visible from the beach, with turtles and easy shore access.

places.name: Havelock Island
places.why: The Andamans' main dive hub, with granite pinnacles, macro life and the region's best-known reef, Barracuda City.

places.name: Netrani Island
places.why: A horseshoe-shaped island off Karnataka with the Arabian Sea's best visibility and occasional whale shark passes.

places.name: Barracuda Point, Sipadan
places.why: An oceanic island wall famous for tornado-like barracuda schools and green turtles sleeping in reef crevices.

places.name: Layang-Layang Atoll
places.why: A remote military-run atoll in the South China Sea where scalloped hammerheads school along the outer wall.

places.name: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
places.why: Two coral atolls in open sea reached only by liveaboard in a short season, with reef sharks and manta on nearly every dive.

places.name: Apo Reef Natural Park
places.why: The Philippines' largest contiguous reef system, a wall dive with grey reef sharks and dense coral cover.

places.name: Monad Shoal
places.why: A seamount where thresher sharks rise from the deep at dawn to be cleaned, one of the only reliable places to see them.

places.name: Anilao
places.why: The Philippines' macro-diving capital, a maze of muck sites packed with nudibranchs and frogfish.

places.name: Coron Bay Wrecks
places.why: A dozen Japanese WWII supply ships sunk in a single 1944 raid, sitting close together in warm, clear bay water.

places.name: USAT Liberty Wreck
places.why: A WWII cargo ship washed ashore by a volcanic eruption, now a shallow, shore-accessible wreck thick with coral and fish.

places.name: Manta Point, Nusa Penida
places.why: A cleaning-station bay where reef manta rays glide close to the surface in surge-heavy, current-fed water.

places.name: Crystal Bay
places.why: A cool-water channel where oceanic sunfish rise from the deep to be cleaned each summer upwelling season.

places.name: Cape Kri
places.why: The site that holds the record for the most fish species logged on a single dive, on a current-fed reef slope.

places.name: Misool
places.why: A no-take marine reserve of limestone islets with soft-coral walls rebuilt from a former shark-finning camp.

places.name: Bunaken Marine Park
places.why: Steep walls dropping into deep water just off a small island, with dense reef fish and clear visibility.

places.name: Lembeh Strait
places.why: The world's best-known muck-diving destination, a black-sand strait crawling with mimic octopus and rare critters.

places.name: Batu Bolong, Komodo
places.why: A small current-battered pinnacle covered edge to edge in soft coral, one of Komodo's most photographed dives.

places.name: Wakatobi
places.why: A remote reef system with some of Indonesia's healthiest coral cover, built around a private no-fishing zone.

places.name: Alor
places.why: A cold, nutrient-rich strait with critter-filled muck sites and dramatic drop-offs in the same small area.

places.name: Similan Islands
places.why: Granite boulder formations underwater mirroring the islands above, with whale sharks passing on migration.

places.name: Richelieu Rock
places.why: A submerged horseshoe pinnacle thick with soft coral, regularly visited by whale sharks in season.

places.name: Hin Daeng & Hin Muang
places.why: A pair of pinnacles, one pink coral and one purple soft coral, with manta and whale shark visits in deep blue water.

places.name: Chumphon Pinnacle
places.why: A submerged granite pinnacle off Koh Tao known for whale shark encounters and schooling barracuda.

places.name: Sail Rock
places.why: A pinnacle with a vertical swim-through chimney and some of the Gulf of Thailand's most reliable whale shark sightings.

places.name: Cham Islands
places.why: A small marine protected area off central Vietnam with coral gardens far healthier than the mainland coast.

places.name: Hin Bida
places.why: A dome-shaped reef off the Phi Phi islands with leopard sharks resting on the sand and dense reef fish.

places.name: King Cruiser Wreck
places.why: A car ferry that sank in 1997 between two reefs, now an easy wreck dive for recreational divers.

places.name: Blue Corner
places.why: A current-swept wall corner where divers reef-hook in to watch grey reef sharks and schooling barracuda hang in the current.

places.name: German Channel
places.why: A hand-dug channel through the reef that funnels manta rays past a cleaning station most of the year.

places.name: Jellyfish Lake
places.why: A marine lake where millions of stingless golden jellyfish migrate daily, snorkelled rather than scuba dived.

places.name: Yap
places.why: Channel cleaning stations where reef manta rays can be seen year-round without a boat ride into open ocean.

places.name: Chuuk Lagoon
places.why: A WWII naval base sunk in a single 1944 air raid, now the world's largest collection of diveable wrecks in one lagoon.

places.name: Bikini Atoll
places.why: Nuclear test wrecks including a sunken aircraft carrier, dived by a handful of technical liveaboards each year.

places.name: Apra Harbor Wrecks
places.why: A rare harbour where a Japanese and an American WWII wreck lie close enough to touch on the same dive.

places.name: SS Yongala
places.why: A 1911 passenger steamer sunk by a cyclone, now an intact 90m wreck acting as an artificial reef in open water.

places.name: Cod Hole
places.why: A famous hand-feeding site for giant, tame potato cod on the outer Great Barrier Reef.

places.name: Osprey Reef
places.why: An isolated ribbon reef rising from 1000m of water, with sheer walls and reliable shark action at North Horn.

places.name: Ningaloo Reef
places.why: A fringing reef reachable straight off the beach, with a reliable whale shark season each austral autumn.

places.name: Rowley Shoals
places.why: Three isolated coral atolls on the edge of the continental shelf, pristine and rarely dived outside a short season.

places.name: Julian Rocks
places.why: A rocky outcrop where warm and cold currents meet, mixing tropical and temperate species including grey nurse sharks.

places.name: Lord Howe Island
places.why: The world's southernmost coral reef, a volcanic remnant with clear water and an easy-going, low-key dive scene.

places.name: Christmas Island
places.why: A steep volcanic island with a short but reliable whale shark season and walls dropping straight into deep water.

places.name: Poor Knights Islands
places.why: Subtropical volcanic pinnacles and archways carrying warm-current fish life far south of the tropics, in a strict no-take reserve.

places.name: Milford Sound
places.why: A dark, tannin-stained fjord where black coral grows in unusually shallow water, normally found only much deeper.

places.name: Goat Island Marine Reserve
places.why: New Zealand's first marine reserve, with snapper and crayfish that show little fear of divers after decades of protection.

places.name: Flinders Reef
places.why: A subtropical bommie reef with leopard sharks and manta cleaning stations closer to Brisbane than the Barrier Reef.

places.name: Neptune Islands
places.why: The world's most reliable cage-diving site for great white sharks, in cold Southern Ocean water.

places.name: Doubtful Sound
places.why: A remote fjord with the same shallow black-coral phenomenon as Milford Sound but far fewer visitors.

places.name: Great Astrolabe Reef
places.why: One of the world's largest barrier reefs, a soft-coral wall system with manta cleaning stations and few crowds.

places.name: Beqa Lagoon
places.why: A shallow sand arena where up to eight shark species, including bull sharks, are fed under strict conservation management.

places.name: Rainbow Reef
places.why: Fiji's Soft Coral Capital, a current-fed strait where the reef is carpeted in every colour of soft coral.

places.name: SS President Coolidge
places.why: A converted WWII troopship that struck mines and sank almost intact, one of the world's largest accessible wreck dives.

places.name: Million Dollar Point
places.why: A shore dump of WWII military vehicles and equipment bulldozed into the sea at the end of the Pacific campaign.

places.name: Bonegi Beach Wrecks
places.why: Japanese transport ships beached and sunk during the WWII Guadalcanal campaign, dived straight from shore.

places.name: Kimbe Bay
places.why: A volcanic bay with an exceptional density of reef types packed into a small area, from Walindi's original dive resort.

places.name: Milne Bay
places.why: The birthplace of muck diving, with black-sand slopes crowded with rare critters near WWII wreck sites.

places.name: Molokini Crater
places.why: A crescent-shaped volcanic caldera protecting exceptionally clear water and a back wall dropping to open ocean.

places.name: Cathedrals, Lanai
places.why: Lava-tube caverns with shafts of light streaming through the ceiling, one of Hawaii's most scenic dives.

places.name: Manta Night Dive, Kona
places.why: Lights on the seabed draw plankton, and plankton draws giant manta rays that feed just above the divers.

places.name: North Shore Shark Dive
places.why: An open-ocean cage-free encounter with Galapagos and sandbar sharks a few miles off Oahu's North Shore.

places.name: Yonaguni Monument
places.why: Controversial stepped rock formations that draw both divers and archaeologists, plus seasonal hammerhead schools.

places.name: Manta Scramble
places.why: A cleaning station reef where reef manta rays gather reliably enough to headline the island's whole dive industry.

places.name: Osezaki
places.why: A muck-diving point on a narrow spit, Japan's best-known shore dive for critters and seasonal migratory fish.

places.name: Munseom Island
places.why: A protected volcanic islet off Korea's southern coast with soft coral gardens at the edge of their range.

places.name: Compass Cay
places.why: A shallow marina cut where docile nurse sharks gather, alongside the Exumas' clear cays and blue holes.

places.name: Grand Turk Wall
places.why: A wall beginning just 90m offshore, plunging to 2,100m and passing migrating humpback whales in winter.

places.name: French Cay
places.why: An uninhabited cay ringed by a coral wall known for reef sharks and consistently good visibility.

places.name: Deception Island
places.why: A flooded volcanic caldera where drysuit divers descend past steaming black-sand vents in near-freezing water.

places.name: Farasan Islands
places.why: A remote Saudi archipelago with pristine reef largely untouched by mass tourism, opened to diving in recent years.

places.name: Fujairah Wrecks
places.why: A cluster of scuttled ships on the UAE's east coast, accessible on day boats from Dubai and Fujairah.

places.name: Sodwana Bay
places.why: South Africa's most popular reef dive base, with the world's southernmost coral reefs and regular ragged-tooth sharks.

places.name: Blue Bay Marine Park
places.why: A shallow lagoon reserve with glass-bottom-boat coral gardens and an easy introduction to Mauritius diving.

places.name: Rodrigues Island
places.why: An isolated volcanic island with its own barrier reef, less developed and less dived than the Mauritius mainland.

places.name: Barren Island
places.why: India's only active volcano, its underwater slopes covered in black volcanic sand and pioneer coral growth.

places.name: Pigeon Island National Park
places.why: A shallow reef park on the northeast coast with blacktip reef sharks patrolling close to shore.

places.name: Japanese Wreck, Amed
places.why: A small WWII patrol boat sitting just off a black-sand beach, an easy, shallow shore dive.

places.name: Shark Point, Gili Trawangan
places.why: A drift dive over a sloping reef where reef sharks and turtles rest among the rubble and coral bommies.

places.name: Sangalaki Island
places.why: A manta ray cleaning station and green turtle nesting beach off Borneo, reached via the Derawan liveaboard route.

places.name: Burma Banks
places.why: A submerged reef system in a remote archipelago only opened to diving in the 1990s, with big pelagic passes.

places.name: Black Rock, Mergui
places.why: An isolated pinnacle in Myanmar's remote archipelago, known for manta rays and near-total lack of crowds.

places.name: Gato Island
places.why: A small island with a swim-through tunnel and resting whitetip reef sharks, paired with nearby Monad Shoal.

places.name: Sardine Run, Moalboal
places.why: A resident bait ball of millions of sardines that sits over the same shallow reef year-round, visible from shore.

places.name: Mabul Island
places.why: A muck-diving island near Sipadan known for frogfish, mandarinfish and a resident population of seahorses.

places.name: Tioman Island
places.why: A volcanic island in the South China Sea with granite boulder reefs, popular for beginner and intermediate divers.

places.name: Blue Holes
places.why: A set of vertical shafts opening onto the outer reef wall next to Blue Corner, one of Palau's classic swim-throughs.

places.name: Peleliu Wall
places.why: A World War II battlefield island with a sheer wall dive on strong currents at the edge of the reef shelf.

places.name: Rainbow Warrior Wreck
places.why: Greenpeace's flagship, bombed in 1985 and later scuttled as a memorial reef dive in the Cavalli Islands.

places.name: Flowerpot Island, Fathom Five
places.why: Freshwater wreck diving in Georgian Bay, with 19th-century schooners preserved by the Great Lakes' cold water.

places.name: USS Monitor
places.why: The Civil War ironclad that sank in a storm in 1862, now a protected wreck in the Graveyard of the Atlantic.

places.name: Banco Chinchorro
places.why: Mexico's largest atoll, a shipwreck graveyard on a barrier reef far enough offshore to stay wonderfully undived.

places.name: Mohéli Marine Park
places.why: A little-known marine park between Madagascar and Africa with turtles, dugong and untouched reef.

places.name: Saint-Gilles-les-Bains Reef
places.why: A fringing lagoon reef off a French volcanic island, one of the few reef dives in this part of the southwest Indian Ocean.

places.name: Tiputa Pass
places.why: A rip-current pass between lagoon and ocean where hundreds of grey sharks stack up to ride the incoming tide.

places.name: Fakarava South Pass
places.why: A UNESCO biosphere pass holding the world's largest documented aggregation of grey reef sharks.

places.name: Bora Bora Lagoon
places.why: A shallow, current-free lagoon where blacktip reef sharks and stingrays can be seen on an easy introductory dive.

places.name: Prony Bay
places.why: A sheltered bay in the world's largest lagoon, known for seasonal humpback whales and easy, calm diving.

places.name: Niue
places.why: A raised coral atoll nation with some of the clearest water on Earth and a resident population of banded sea snakes.

places.name: Flower Garden Banks
